title: Build a hand: 21 is not always blackjack
subtitle: 2 introductions · 5 practice · 5 independent tasks

theory.text: The goal is to beat the dealer without busting, not to keep drawing until 21. An ace is 1 or 11; J, Q and K are 10. Assemble each hand one card at a time. Classify the completed hand: natural blackjack is an ace plus a ten-value card in the original two-card hand; three-card 21 and 21 after a split are not natural blackjack. More than 21 is bust. A hand below 21 is still in play, but this does not mean you should hit. Even 21 is no promise of a win: the dealer can tie, and a dealer natural beats ordinary 21. Try two guided hands and then ten scored tasks. Only your first answer counts.

theory.text: Build the hand and enter its total. Cards 2–10 keep their number; J, Q and K each count as 10. Count every ace as 1 first, then add 10 if that still fits within 21. Thus A+7 is 18, but adding 9 changes the ace to 1 and gives 17, not 27. With several aces, at most one can count as 11. If even all aces as 1 give more than 21, enter that bust total. Two guided hands show the changing sum; in the ten scored hands the sum stays hidden until feedback or a practice hint. Adjust your total with the buttons, then check it.

coaching.contrast: Compare A+7 = 18 with A+7+9 = 17: adding a card can reduce the total when the ace changes value.

mistakes.total: That total does not match. Add the numbers, replace face cards with 10 and check each ace.

theory.text: A soft hand has an ace currently worth 11. A hard hand has no ace worth 11, even if it contains one or more aces. Build the cards in order: A+6 is soft 17; add K and it becomes hard 17 because the ace drops to 1. A+A+8 is soft 20, but A+A+9+9 is hard 20: both aces must be 1. Classify the final hand, not the hand before the last card. The guided examples reveal the total and type after each card. Practice hints and feedback explain the transition; the five independent tasks give no hints.

scenarios.prompt: Build the hand. After the last card, is it soft or hard?

coaching.explanation: Total 17. One ace can still count as 11 without exceeding 21, so the final hand is soft.
coaching.contrast: Compare A+6 (soft 17) with A+6+10 (hard 17): the total matches but the ace value changes.

mistakes.hard: Check whether you can add 10 to the all-aces-as-1 total without busting.
mistakes.soft: An ace alone does not make a hand soft. It must currently count as 11.

theory.text: Follow the instruction and try each control; this lesson tests action meanings, not the best strategy. Hit adds a card. Stand keeps the hand as it is. Double doubles the round stake, adds exactly one card and ends that hand. Split separates a pair into two hands. Late Surrender ends the original hand with half the stake lost, after the dealer has checked for blackjack. In our 6D/S17/DAS/late-surrender/peek/3:2 profile, Double and Surrender need two cards; Surrender is unavailable after Split, but Double is allowed after splitting non-aces. Split aces receive one card each and stop. Unavailable controls remain disabled. Each successful action shows a fixed demonstration, not a random win or a real wager.

scenarios.prompt: Add another card without doubling.

coaching.explanation: Hit adds the demonstrated card. On a hand with three or more cards, Double and Surrender are no longer available.
coaching.contrast: Compare: Hit permits another decision if the hand remains live; Double adds one card and stops. Stand adds no cards; Surrender fixes a half-stake loss.
